title: Mid-circuit measurements and feedforward implement every unitary exactly in constant depth
abstract: Mid-circuit measurements with feedforward reduce the optimal worst-case quantum depth for exact $n$-qubit unitary synthesis from $Θ(n)$ to $O(1)$, using arbitrary one- and two-qubit gates and unrestricted ancillary space. Measurements and resets without feedforward remain subject to the circuit causal-cone bound. Our deterministic construction uses single-qubit measurements, $O(1)$ rounds of parity feedforward, and $O(n4^n\log(n+2))$ total qubits, with all ancillas starting and ending in $|0\rangle$. Classical processing is not counted in quantum depth. We teleport only the matrix error of an approximation by Nehoran and Yuen. An exactly prepared ancillary state encodes this error, whose action is added back by coherent interference. At operator-norm error $2^{-n}$, one step of amplitude amplification suffices. Coherent fanout circuits achieve the same constant-depth bound, while circuits using only one- and two-qubit gates attain depth $Θ(n)$ with $O(4^n\log^2(n+2))$ gates. Generic targets require $Ω(4^n/(h+1))$ qubits at depth $h$, even under unrestricted classical control. Our depth-width trade-offs meet this bound within a factor $O(n^2)$ for $1\le h\le2^n$.
summary: This paper presents a breakthrough in quantum circuit synthesis, demonstrating that by incorporating mid-circuit measurements and feedforward, the depth required to implement any $n$-qubit unitary can be reduced to a constant depth, $O(1)$. This significantly improves upon previous bounds of $\Theta(n)$ depth. The results establish powerful depth-width trade-offs for quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental question of determining the minimum quantum depth required for the exact synthesis of an arbitrary $n$-qubit unitary operation.
main_result: Mid-circuit measurements combined with feedforward reduce the optimal worst-case quantum depth for exact unitary synthesis from $\Theta(n)$ to $O(1)$.
method: The authors employ techniques like residual repair, coherent interference, and deterministic constructions utilizing single-qubit measurements and parity feedforward.
model_or_system: The model is quantum computation using $n$ input qubits and ancillary qubits, allowing arbitrary one- and two-qubit gates with all-to-all connectivity.
key_observables: Quantum depth ($h$), circuit width ($w$), and the error norm ($\|U - eU\|$).
important_parameters: The number of qubits ($n$), the target unitary dimension ($d$), and the depth/width trade-off exponent.
main_assumptions: The construction assumes unrestricted ancillary space and relies on the ability to prepare the residual state exactly.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the 'Residual repair' process, comparing direct Choi encoding methods with the improved residual-based method, and show the depth-width landscape for various synthesis bounds.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing general depth-width trade-offs (Theorem 7) to introducing the residual repair technique (Theorem 2), and culminates in the constant-depth construction using measurement and feedforward (Theorem 1).
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental, resource-efficient circuit blueprints for universal quantum computation, which is crucial for designing hardware-efficient quantum algorithms.
